`user-cert.der` is the public X.509 certificate from
`../../../../../ofdrw-sign/src/test/resources/USER.p12`. The Java
`DigitalSignContainerTest` uses that PKCS#12 file to sign `DigitalSign.ofd`.
`user-private-key.bin` is the matching 32-byte private scalar extracted from
that same Java test-only PKCS#12 file. It is used only for signing integration
tests and must never be used outside tests.
`root-cert.der` is the public certificate from
`../../../../../ofdrw-gm/src/main/resources/ROOT.p12`. Its KeyUsage omits
`keyCertSign`, so it is a negative test for strict CA checks.
`trust-root-cert.der`, `trust-leaf-cert.der`, and
`trust-leaf-private-key.bin` form a separate SM2 test chain generated with
OpenSSL 3. The root has `CA:TRUE` and `keyCertSign`; the leaf has
`digitalSignature`. The leaf scalar is test-only and must never be used outside
tests. Only the public certificates are needed for chain verification.
`chain-root-cert.der`, `chain-intermediate-cert.der`, `chain-leaf-cert.der`,
and `chain-leaf-private-key.bin` form a separate OpenSSL 3 SM2 test chain.
The root allows one intermediate CA (`pathLenConstraint=1`), while the
intermediate allows none (`pathLenConstraint=0`). The leaf scalar is test-only.
Certificate signatures in this chain use an empty SM2 distinguishing ID.

`swapped-rg.icc` is a 588-byte test profile generated from LittleCMS
`cmsCreate_sRGBProfile`; the `rXYZ` and `gXYZ` tag offsets were exchanged.
It makes an RGB red input render green, so tests detect whether ICC conversion
actually occurs.
`gamma18-rgb.icc` and `gamma18-gray.icc` are small test profiles generated
with LittleCMS `cmsCreateRGBProfile` and `cmsCreateGrayProfile` using a gamma
of 1.8. They exercise 16-bit conversion and GRAY profile handling.
`snap-newsprint-cmyk.icc` is the SNAP TR002 newsprint CMYK profile distributed
with colord (`data/profiles/SNAP_TR002_newsprint.icc`, CC0-1.0). It verifies
four-channel JPEG sample conversion through an embedded PDF ICC color space.
`cmyk-icc-jpeg.pdf` is generated by `scripts/generate_link_fixtures.py` from
that profile and `cmyk.jpg`; its image uses `/Decode [1 0]` for each channel.
`ycck.jpg` is generated by `scripts/generate_ycck_jpeg.c` with libjpeg-turbo
and contains red and black Adobe YCCK samples. `ycck-icc-jpeg.pdf` embeds it
with the same ICC profile and `/Decode` array.
`cmyk-mask.pdf`, `ycck-mask.pdf`, and their `-decode-mask` variants are generated
by `scripts/generate_cmyk_mask_fixtures.py`. They embed those JPEGs in
DeviceCMYK image XObjects with a color-key `/Mask` that hides the red pixel and
leaves the black pixel visible. The variants also invert all four channels
through `/Decode`. Rust, Python, and Go tests check import and package round
trips; Rust and Go also inspect the resulting alpha samples.
`kerning-simhei.ttf` is derived from the repository's
`ofdrw-layout/src/test/resources/simhei-cut1.ttf`. It adds a legacy `kern`
table with a -64 font-unit adjustment for the `HW` glyph pair. The source font
uses 256 units per em. This small fixture makes pair positioning deterministic
across Rust, C, Python, and Go tests.
`dejavu-serif.ttf` is the DejaVu Serif font distributed with Ubuntu's
`fonts-dejavu-core` package. `dejavu-copyright.txt` contains its copyright and
license terms. Its `fi` ligature exercises OFD `CGTransform` writing and
rendering with a stable font on every test platform.
`dejavu-sans.ttf` is from the same package and covered by the same license
file. Its Arabic glyphs exercise right-to-left shaping and joined forms.
`dejavu-sans-bold-oblique.ttf` is also from that package under the same license.
Its intrinsic bold and italic flags exercise PDF font style import and reuse.
`font-style-standard.pdf` and `font-style-descriptor.pdf` are generated by
`scripts/generate_font_style_fixture.py`. They preserve the same Chinese text
and explicit advances while declaring styles through a standard font name or
indirect FontDescriptor fields. Python and Node.js check their OFD round trips.
`custom-type1-differences.pdf` is generated by
`scripts/generate_encoding_differences_fixture.py`. It uses a custom subset
font name, explicit widths and an indirect Differences encoding without a
ToUnicode map. Rust, Python, Go and Node.js compare the recovered Chinese text.
`type0-mixed-cmap.pdf` and `type0-four-byte-cmap.pdf` are generated by
`scripts/generate_cid_cmap_fixture.py`. Their compressed Encoding CMaps map
mixed-length source codes to independent CIDs. Tests compare Chinese text,
explicit CID advances, embedded-font reuse and OFD package/render round trips.
`type0-gbk-cmap.pdf`, `type0-cns-cmap.pdf`, `type0-jis-cmap.pdf` and
`type0-ks-cmap.pdf` are generated by `scripts/generate_named_cmap_fixtures.py`.
They use known Adobe GB1/CNS1/Japan1/Korea1 CIDs with distinct source codes,
explicit widths and ToUnicode maps. Rust tests check all four collections;
Python/Go check Chinese cases and Node.js checks all four text samples.
`type0-*-collection-unicode.pdf` files are generated by
`scripts/generate_cid_unicode_fixtures.py`. They omit ToUnicode and recover
registered Adobe collection text, including an Identity-H case whose CIDs
are not Unicode values. The supplementary Japanese collection fixture uses
CID 19130 for U+31350. Rust compares their explicit-map counterparts' geometry
and raster output; Python/Go/Node.js check package round trips.
`type0-ligature-glyph.pdf`, `truetype-ligature-glyph.pdf`,
`type0-variation-glyph.pdf` and `type0-no-unicode-cmap-glyph.pdf` are generated
by `scripts/generate_pdf_glyph_fixtures.py`. They reuse licensed DejaVu Serif
under a checked digest. The first two map one source glyph to `fi`; the
variation case recovers `0` plus VS1 from Adobe-Japan1 CID 230. The last case
removes the sfnt cmap directory entry and repairs the sfnt checksum, leaving
source glyph outlines unchanged. All three bindings verify text, glyph IDs,
rendering and save/reopen. `pdf-ligature-reference.png` is independently rendered
with Ghostscript using the command in that generator's docstring.
`pdf-overhang-reference.png` uses the same source with glyph `j` (GID 77),
whose negative left bearing tests object-boundary expansion. Regenerate both
independent PNGs with `python scripts/generate_pdf_glyph_fixtures.py --references`.
`truetype-macroman.pdf` is generated by `scripts/generate_tounicode_fixture.py`.
It embeds the compressed DejaVu Sans program and uses `MacRomanEncoding` byte
`0x8e` for `é`; Python and Go tests check text and embedded-font round trips.
`negative-horizontal-scale.pdf` is generated by
`scripts/generate_negative_horizontal_scale_fixture.py`. Its Type1 text uses
`-50 Tz` followed by `100 Tz`, so bindings can verify mirrored glyph placement,
positive OFD `HScale`, and the next run's PDF text position.
`optional-content.pdf` comes from the same script. It hides one Type1 text run
through an OFF OCG and shows another through an `AnyOn` OCMD. Python and Go
tests check the visible text after import and OFD save/reopen.
`versioned.ofd` is a small deterministic package containing one `Versions`
entry, a `DocVersion` description, and three listed package files. It tests
version metadata and missing-file validation across the Rust, C, Python, and
Go APIs.
`popup.pdf` is a minimal PDF with a Text annotation and a linked Popup
annotation. `scripts/create_popup_pdf_fixture.py` regenerates it. Python,
Go, and Node.js tests check import and PDF export round trips.
`standalone-popup.pdf` comes from the same script and has an independent Popup
with content and an open state. It tests the independent popup path through the
three bindings.
`ink.pdf` comes from the same script and has two Ink strokes with dashed
border, color, opacity, and author metadata. It tests PDF Ink round trips
through all three bindings.
`polygon.pdf` and `polyline.pdf` come from the same generator. They exercise
vertex geometry, fill versus line-ending color, and dimension intent.

`rotate-90.pdf`, `rotate-180.pdf`, and `rotate-270.pdf` are small generated
PDF 1.6 files with a nonzero MediaBox origin, `/UserUnit 2`, a non-square
page, a vector fill and stroke, Type1 text, and an RGB image. The 90-degree
fixture also clips its stroke. They test page rotation and imported object
geometry across the bindings and Java reader.
`page-group-rotated-text.pdf` is a minimal PDF 1.7 page with an RGB
transparency group, a 90-degree page rotation, a red vector path, and Type1
text with an independent rotation matrix. It checks both page group parsing
and composition of page and object transforms across language bindings.
`named-links.pdf` is generated by `scripts/generate_link_fixtures.py`.
Its two annotations target the same page through a nested `/Names` destination
name tree and a legacy catalog `/Dests` dictionary, respectively.
The same script generates `quad-links.pdf`, whose first link has two
quadrilateral hit regions and whose second link has a direct page destination.
`affine-image.pdf` is a generated PDF 1.4 file containing a mirrored RGB
image on a page rotated 90 degrees. It tests composition of image and page
transforms through the Rust importer and language bindings.
`packed-gray.pdf` is a generated PDF 1.4 file with a 5×2 one-bit grayscale
image, per-row padding, and an inverted `/Decode [1 0]` array. It also tests
that the imported OFD image fills its declared square boundary.
`blend.pdf` is a generated PDF 1.4 file with overlapping black and green
rectangles. Its `/BM /Darken` graphics state applies only inside `q`/`Q`;
binding tests check its imported SVG and PNG output.
`text-clip.pdf` is a generated PDF 1.4 file whose Type1 `Tr 7` text object
contains two text runs. The glyph outlines clip the following red rectangle;
`Q` restores the clip before a green rectangle is drawn.
`soft-mask.pdf` is a generated PDF 1.4 file with a 2×2 RGB image and a
grayscale `/SMask` image whose samples are 0, 128, and 255. Bindings verify
the imported PNG alpha channel and package round trip.
`color-key-mask.pdf` derives from `image.pdf` by adding
`/Mask [255 255 0 0 0 0]` to its 2×2 RGB image. Bindings verify that the red
sample becomes transparent while the green sample remains opaque.
`red-blue-32x32.jp2` and `gray16-pair-32x32.jp2` are lossless JPEG2000 images
with two source colors. They test 8-bit RGB and 16-bit grayscale color-key
comparisons. `scripts/generate_jpx_color_key_fixture.py` embeds the RGB image
in `red-blue-jpx-mask.pdf` for language-binding import tests.
`explicit-mask.pdf` is a generated PDF 1.4 file with a 2×2 RGB image and a
separate one-bit `/ImageMask true` image referenced through `/Mask`. Its mask
bits alternate opaque and transparent pixels in both rows.
`stencil-mask.pdf` is a generated PDF 1.4 file that paints a 2×2 one-bit
`/ImageMask true` XObject directly, using green as the current nonstroking
color. Its pixels alternate painted and transparent in both rows.
`image-mask.ofd` has a 2×1 red/blue image and a white/black `ImageMask` PNG.
Its expected preview is red/transparent before the page's white background.
Its `DocID` is a 32-digit hexadecimal UUID so document validation has no
unrelated metadata issue.

`java-cert-encrypted.ofd` was produced by Java
`OFDEncryptorTest#encryptCert` from `ofdrw-crypto/src/test/resources/hello.ofd`
using its `sign_cert.pem`. `java-sm2-cert.der` is the DER form of that PEM
certificate; `java-sm2-private-key.bin` is its 32-byte SM2 private scalar.
`rust-cert-encrypted.ofd` was produced by the Rust `encrypt_certificate`
example with the same source document and certificate. These test-only keys
and packages verify certificate decryption in both directions.
`java-mixed-encrypted.ofd` is produced by `RustMixedInteropTest#javaWritesMixedPackage`
with a password user and an SM2 certificate user. `rust-mixed-encrypted.ofd`
is produced by the Rust `encrypt_mixed` example from the same source document.
Both are read with either credential in interoperability tests.
`type1-tounicode.pdf` is generated by
`scripts/generate_tounicode_fixture.py`. Its Type1 font maps the bytes `AB`
to `中文` through a one-byte `ToUnicode` CMap while `/Widths` and a `TJ`
adjustment control the original glyph advance.
`type1-subset-tounicode.pdf` is generated by the same script. It uses a
nonstandard subset font name and an `Encoding` dictionary with `Differences`;
its complete `ToUnicode` CMap supplies the imported Unicode text.
`rotated-tounicode.pdf` uses the same one-byte mapping with a 90-degree PDF
text matrix; import should preserve its baseline, rotation, and glyph spacing.
`metadata-tounicode.pdf` adds UTF-16 PDF Info strings, a keyword string, and
PDF creation/modification dates to the same text content.
`outline-tounicode.pdf` adds a nested PDF outline tree with a collapsed parent,
Unicode title, direct `Fit`/`XYZ` destinations, and a `GoTo` action.
`type0-identity-tounicode.pdf` is generated by the same script. It has a
two-byte `Identity-H` CID font, a `ToUnicode` CMap, and descendant `W` widths;
all six fixtures should import as the same `中文` text.
`shading-axial.pdf` is a minimal PDF 1.4 page with a half-page clipped red-to-blue
axial shading, a type 2 linear function, and both endpoint extension flags.
`shading-bbox.pdf` adds a `BBox` and a separate current clipping path whose
intersection is visible. Its green `Background` must be ignored by `sh`.
`shading-radial.pdf` and `shading-radial-reverse.pdf` contain nested concentric
circle shadings whose radii grow and shrink, respectively. Reproducible source
is in `scripts/generate_shading_fixtures.py`.
`shading-stitching.pdf` uses a type 3 stitching function with two type 2
subfunctions, a discontinuity at `Bounds [0.5]`, and a reversed second `Encode`
interval.
`shading-domain.pdf` and `shading-stitching-domain.pdf` limit the same
functions to `Domain [0.25 0.75]`, so endpoint colors and stitching bounds
must be remapped to the OFD gradient axis.
`shading-range.pdf` and `shading-stitching-range.pdf` exercise a type 2
function `Range` that clips output colors into flat intervals before and
after a linear transition, both directly and inside a stitching function.
`shading-cmyk-range.pdf` adds a four-channel range and a combined cyan/black
ink threshold at the gradient midpoint.
`shading-extend-{none,start,end,both}.pdf` use the same short axial gradient
axis with each PDF `Extend` combination, leaving visible page margins for
pixel checks.
`xobject-associated-files.pdf` has a page Form XObject containing a one-pixel
RGB image XObject. Each XObject has an `AF` file specification with an embedded
payload, and there is no `EmbeddedFiles` name tree. It is generated by
`scripts/generate_xobject_associated_files_fixture.py`.

The `test-*-cff.otf` and `test-*.cff` fonts and their `type*-cff.pdf`/PNG
fixtures are authored by `scripts/generate_cff_pdf_fixtures.py` under this
repository's Apache-2.0 license. They contain three synthetic glyph outlines,
including a curved ligature and a CID charset whose CIDs differ from GIDs.
The generator needs fonttools; normal tests use the checked-in fixtures.
PNG references are generated independently with Ghostscript at 72 DPI.

Affine CFF cases cover top-level skew, reflection, rotation, translation,
per-FD inheritance with FDSelect formats 0 and 3, vertical layout, strokes and
text clipping. `type0-clipped-ligature.pdf` uses the existing DejaVu Serif
fixture to check the same mapped-glyph clipping path for TrueType fonts.

`mesh-*.pdf` and PNG references are authored by
`scripts/generate_mesh_shading_fixtures.py`. They cover PDF free-form/lattice
Gouraud shading, byte padding, 32-bit coordinates, 16-bit colors, nonlinear
CMYK/CalGray conversion, four function types and component-function arrays,
transforms, clips, alpha and blend modes. References use Ghostscript at 72 DPI.
The DeviceCMYK reference uses `-dUseFastColor` to select simple subtractive
conversion rather than a machine's default CMYK ICC profile, as described in
[Ghostscript's color options](https://ghostscript.readthedocs.io/en/master/Use.html#dUseFastColor).

`patch-*.pdf` and PNG references are authored by
`scripts/generate_patch_shading_fixtures.py`. They exercise PDF Coons and tensor
patches, packed fields and nonzero byte-padding, three shared-edge modes, curved and folded
surfaces, corner-color functions, clipping, opacity and transforms. Ghostscript
produces the independent 72-DPI references; ordinary tests run entirely offline.

`plane-*.pdf` and PNG references are authored by
`scripts/generate_plane_shading_fixtures.py`. They exercise PDF Type 1 shading,
two-input sampled/calculator functions, component arrays, three-point and
multidimensional cubic interpolation, packed data, discontinuities, reversed
mappings, CalGray/CMYK conversion and domain/matrix/clip mapping. Independent
72-DPI references use Ghostscript; the CMYK case uses `-dUseFastColor` for the
same simple subtractive device-color conversion used by the importer.

`separation-*.pdf` and PNG references are authored by
`scripts/generate_separation_fixtures.py` (Pillow is needed only to generate
the grayscale JPEG). Eighteen cases exercise alternate colors, four function
types, Indexed palettes, images, color-key masking, All/None and shadings.
Ghostscript renders the references at 72 DPI. Three oracle inputs independently
expand normative semantics to avoid Ghostscript 10.02.1 discrepancies: the
stitching boundary uses explicit RGB (ISO 32000-1 7.10.4), the 16-bit color-key
predicate uses an explicit alpha mask (8.9.6.4), and None uses background only
(8.6.6.4). The original PDFs remain the importer inputs. Separate semantic
assertions verify None text retention, clipping and independent RGB content.
The Indexed image has one sample per output pixel to avoid conflating palette
conversion with differences in image resampling between renderers.

`devicen-*.pdf` and PNG references are authored by
`scripts/generate_device_n_fixtures.py`. Eighteen cases cover multi-input
calculator and sampled/cubic transforms, RGB/CMYK alternates, three-input
functions, two/five/32-channel images, 16-bit color-key masking, Indexed bases,
all/mixed None, clipping, NChannel composite fallback and four shading families.
References use Ghostscript at 72 DPI (`-dUseFastColor` for CMYK). As with the
Separation fixtures, the all-None oracle contains only the unchanged background,
and the 16-bit mask oracle expands the raw-sample predicate into explicit alpha.
The importer always receives the original PDF. Tests separately inspect the
original image alpha samples and retained None text. No generator is required
for ordinary offline tests.

`devicen-jpx-*.pdf` and PNG references are authored by
`scripts/generate_multichannel_jpx_fixtures.py`, using glymur/numpy/packaging
and OpenJPEG only during generation. The ten cases encode lossless
2/4/5/32-component codestreams, container color overrides, embedded alpha,
8/16-bit color-key masking, external soft masks and omitted `BitsPerComponent`. Ghostscript generates 72-DPI references.
For Ghostscript 10.02.1, the omitted-bit-depth oracle supplies redundant
`BitsPerComponent` metadata (ISO 32000-1 Table 89 requires readers to determine
JPX precision from the codestream); the 16-bit color-key oracle expands its
raw-sample predicate into explicit alpha, as in the other tint fixtures.
The container-color oracle uses the same encoded samples without its embedded
RGB color declaration: PDF's explicit `ColorSpace` takes precedence over it
(ISO 32000-1 Table 89). Tests also require byte-identical converted images
between these inputs and when redundant bit-depth/Decode metadata changes.
Original PDFs remain the importer inputs, and tests inspect alpha samples
independently. Ordinary tests use the checked-in files without those tools.

`intent-test-cmyk.icc` is authored under Apache-2.0 by
`scripts/generate_intent_profile.py`. Its ICC v2 LUT8 tables produce different
constant neutral Lab values for perceptual, relative-colorimetric and saturation
conversion, making rendering-intent inheritance observable independently of
source samples. The tests compare converted pixels across graphics states,
image-level overrides and masking paths.

`image-intent-*.pdf` and PNG references are authored by
`scripts/generate_image_intent_fixtures.py` using the synthetic intent profile.
Eight cases exercise `ri`, ExtGState `RI`, q/Q restoration, image Intent
overrides, nested Form resources, raw/Flate inline images, pixel bytes containing
an apparent EI marker, CR pixel data followed by LF separators, and soft/stencil masks. Independent Ghostscript 72-DPI
references use `-dBlackPtComp=0` to match the importer's default color-conversion
setting; [Ghostscript enables black-point compensation by default](https://ghostscript.readthedocs.io/en/gs10.02.0/GhostscriptColorManagement.html). Original
PDFs are rendered directly, without replacement oracle inputs.

`pdf-text-fallback.ttf` is generated by
`scripts/generate_pdf_text_fallback_font.py` using fonttools. Its three distinct
geometric glyphs map U+4E2D, U+6587, and U+31350 for semantic PDF extraction
tests. The outlines are authored under this repository's Apache-2.0 license;
they are not readable Chinese glyphs. Tests embed it to avoid depending on
system CJK fonts. Missing-font rendering and `.notdef` Unicode collisions remain
separate production limitations.

`actual-text-cff.pdf` is generated by `scripts/generate_actual_text_fixture.py`
using the repository-authored CFF outlines from `generate_cff_pdf_fixtures.py`
(Apache-2.0). A Span ActualText string replaces the two painted text runs with
“中文”. Native import and Python/Go/Node tests check replacement text, original
paint and repeated OFD/PDF round trips without requiring readable CJK glyphs.
